correctness.rationale: Direct 3x3 first-step reconstruction gives the displayed rational expression and positive denominators on all r>=0. Coefficient comparison gives the exact difference as a strictly positive prefactor times a quadratic bracket. When U differs the bracket is strictly monotone; when U agrees it is constant. The endpoint and equal-product cases and exact positive-rate witness are proved. Independent exact rational replay covers 3125 first-step cases, 729 polynomial identities and five witness values; finite tests only supplement the full proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is a global one-crossing theorem in regional catastrophe intensity for two-patch Markov metapopulations with both death-rate and colonization-rate totals held fixed, plus explicit sharp switching designs. Existing catastrophe extinction scaling for one population and qualitative or intervention-based patch-model studies do not, on inspected portions, imply this exact threshold classification. The method of linear first-step equations is known. Some primary text remained inaccessible, so residual possibility of equivalent earlier coverage is explicitly acknowledged.

value.rationale: Matched aggregate local death and rescue rates represent a natural fixed-budget ecological design comparison. The exact sign factorization rules out more than one preference reversal as the common-catastrophe hazard varies while an explicit feasible matched-budget pair realizes one genuine reversal. It quantifies when optimizing survival under rare catastrophes can contradict optimizing it under frequent ones. This is structurally meaningful beyond the numerical example, without pretending it predicts larger networks or measured ecosystems.
